record.original_question: For the two 2006 reliability models with state variables Q0(x,t) through Q4(x,t) and P0(x,t) through P6(x,t), representing systems attended by a repairman with vacations and involving boundary conditions such as Q0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) Q0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) Q3(x,t) dx + delta(t) and P0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) P0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) P3(x,t) dx + delta(t), where lambda is the working rate, mu(x) is the repair rate, and alpha(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, determine whether these two PDE models are well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of their time-dependent solutions when alpha(x) and mu(x) are non-constant functions.

evidence.quote: Here (x, t) in [x, infinity) x [0, infinity); Qi(x, t) (i = 0, 1, 2) is the probability that at time t the system is normal and the elapsed vacation time of repairman is x; Qi(x, t) (i = 3, 4) is the probability that at time t the system is down and the elapsed repair time of the piece is x; lambda is the working rate, mu(x) is the repair rate, alpha(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, delta(.) is the Dirac-delta function.
When alpha(x) and mu(x) are non-constants, well-posendess and asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solutions of the above two models have not been obtained until today.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two reliability models for a single-unit (or two-unit) repairable system attended by a repairman who takes vacations. Time t ≥ 0 and elapsed-time variable x ≥ 0 are continuous. Let λ > 0 be the constant working (failure) rate of the system, μ(x) ≥ 0 the repair rate function (depending on the elapsed repair time x), and α(x) ≥ 0 the vacation rate function of the repairman (depending on the elapsed vacation time x). All rate functions are measurable and satisfy ∫₀^∞ μ(x) dx = ∫₀^∞ α(x) dx = +∞.

Model A. Let Q_i(x,t), i = 0,1,2,3,4, be probability densities, where Q_i(x,t) (i = 0,1,2) denotes the probability that at time t the system is in operating state i and the elapsed vacation time of the repairman is x, and Q_i(x,t) (i = 3,4) the probability that at time t the system is down in state i and the elapsed repair time is x. The state functions satisfy a coupled system of first-order linear hyperbolic PDEs of the form
   ∂Q_i/∂t + ∂Q_i/∂x = −(λ + α(x)) Q_i  (i = 0,1,2),
   ∂Q_j/∂t + ∂Q_j/∂x = −μ(x) Q_j        (j = 3,4),
together with appropriate linear couplings between the equations, and with the boundary conditions
   Q_0(0,t) = ∫₀^∞ α(x) Q_0(x,t) dx + ∫₀^∞ μ(x) Q_3(x,t) dx + δ(t),
   Q_i(0,t) = (linear functionals of the Q_k(·,t)),  i = 1,2,3,4,
where δ(·) is the Dirac delta and the initial data correspond to the system starting in state 0 at t = 0.

Model B. Let P_i(x,t), i = 0,1,…,6, be analogous probability densities for a more elaborate variant of the same scheme, satisfying a coupled hyperbolic PDE system of the same type with boundary condition
   P_0(0,t) = ∫₀^∞ α(x) P_0(x,t) dx + ∫₀^∞ μ(x) P_3(x,t) dx + δ(t)
and analogous boundary conditions for P_1,…,P_6.

Assume α(x) and μ(x) are non-constant (i.e., not almost-everywhere constant) functions.

Questions:
(1) Are Models A and B well posed in a suitable Banach space (for instance, L¹([0,∞), ℝ^5) and L¹([0,∞), ℝ^7), respectively); that is, does each system admit a unique nonnegative time-dependent solution depending continuously on the initial data?
(2) Determine the asymptotic behavior as t → ∞ of these time-dependent solutions: in particular, do they converge (strongly, or in some weaker sense) to a steady-state solution, and characterize that limit?
artifact.category_tag: Repairable system PDE models with vacations
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns numerous works on well-posedness and asymptotic stability of repairable systems with repairman vacations using C₀-semigroup methods on Banach lattices, but no source explicitly resolving both well-posedness and asymptotic behavior for the specific Yue–Yu–Bao 2006 five-state and seven-state vacation models with non-constant α(x) and μ(x). The problem is stated as still unresolved in the cited material, and no later paper found in the search clearly settles it, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Semigroup method for a deteriorating system with multiple vacations of a repairman
status_evidence.snippet: System equations are transformed into an abstract Cauchy problem on a Banach lattice; existence of unique nonnegative dynamic solution and convergence to steady state are established for a related vacation model.
status_evidence.claim: Related (but distinct) repairman-vacation models have been treated by semigroup methods, indicating an active line of work but not the same five/seven-state Yue 2006 models.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Analysis of a Deteriorating System with Single Vacation of a Repairman
status_evidence.snippet: Studies well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of a single-vacation deteriorating system, distinct from the Yue 2006 five-state and seven-state models.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature handles related models but does not address the specific Yue 2006 models with general non-constant α(x), μ(x).
